name: Speed, Distance, Time, and Unit Conversions
description: Build the basic speed-distance-time relationship and convert safely between common distance, time, and speed units.
script_scope: Teach Distance = Speed × Time, Speed = Distance ÷ Time, and Time = Distance ÷ Speed through concrete journeys. Cover hours and minutes, kilometres and metres, km/hr to m/sec using ×5/18, m/sec to km/hr using ×18/5, metres per minute, and comparing two speeds only after converting them to the same unit. Include quick checks that the answer unit matches the requested quantity.

name: Same Distance: Speed and Time Ratios
description: Use the inverse relationship between speed and time for the same route, including ratio and percentage changes.
script_scope: Teach that for a fixed distance, speed and time are inversely proportional. Cover reversing speed ratios to get time ratios, recovering actual times from a time difference, percentage increases/decreases in speed, fractional-speed changes, distance ratios when time is not equal, and leap-frequency × leap-length speed comparisons. Make learners check that the distance is actually the same before using the inverse shortcut.

name: Average Speed Across a Journey
description: Find average speed from the whole distance and whole time instead of averaging printed speeds blindly.
script_scope: Teach average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Contrast the common wrong arithmetic mean with the correct method. Cover equal-distance two-speed journeys using 2xy/(x+y), equal-time journeys, three or more equal-distance legs, fractional journey splits, mixed travel modes, round-trip distance recovery, and whole-trip averages that include a stop.

name: Stoppages, Rests, and Effective Speed
description: Separate running time from waiting time and count scheduled stops correctly.
script_scope: Teach running speed versus speed including stoppages. Cover stoppage minutes per elapsed hour, stops after fixed distances, rest-after-each-kilometre problems, removing total halt time to recover running speed, equal halts at junctions, fixed stop schedules, effective speed when only part of each hour is spent moving, and whole-trip average speed including stops. Emphasize that no extra stop occurs after reaching the destination.

name: Changed Speed, Early/Late Arrival, and Schedules
description: Translate faster/slower travel into time gains or losses and solve deadline problems.
script_scope: Teach early/late arrival as a fixed-distance time comparison. Cover fractional speed reductions, two-speed early/late conditions, known-distance speed-change equations, late departures with fixed arrival times, percentage speed increases needed to recover a schedule, paired faster/slower conditions that determine original speed and distance, and remaining-speed questions after part of the route has been covered.

name: Relative Speed: Meeting and Separation
description: Track how quickly the gap between two movers closes or grows.
script_scope: Teach relative speed as the rate at which the gap changes: add speeds for opposite directions and subtract for the same direction. Cover separation, simultaneous meeting between two places, meeting-point distance ratios, staggered opposite starts, same-direction gaps, recovering individual speeds from sum/difference meeting information, and checking that meeting distances add to the full route.

name: Delayed Starts, Catch-Up, and Overtaking
description: Turn head starts into distance gaps and solve chases, catches, and overtaking times.
script_scope: Teach pursuit problems as head-start distance ÷ closing speed. Cover delayed runners and vehicles, goods/express train catch-up, thief-police chases, catch locations, clock-time overtaking, shuttle-dog distance during a chase, regularly spaced buses met by a moving person, and long head-start cases that cross clock-hour boundaries.

name: Segmented Journeys and Target Average Speed
description: Break multi-stage trips into pieces and find the speed needed for the remaining distance or target average.
script_scope: Teach each journey stage as its own distance-speed-time block. Cover fixed-distance stages, unknown total distance from route fractions and total time, leftover-distance fraction problems, target overall average speed, speed changing by regular intervals, accident/slowdown delays, equal-distance two-speed totals, and final-stage speed needed to meet a fixed total time.

name: Circular Tracks, Laps, and Repeated Meetings
description: Apply relative speed around a circle for first meetings, overtakes, repeated crossings, and common returns.
script_scope: Teach a circular track as a repeating gap. Cover first meeting from the same point in opposite directions, first overtake in the same direction, repeated meeting counts, simultaneous return to the starting point using LCM of lap times, starts from opposite points, recovery of speeds from same/opposite meeting intervals, mixed track and speed units, and meeting counts over a fixed time window.

name: Special Motion Models: Sound, Escalators, Leaps, and Puzzles
description: Translate unusual motion stories into ordinary rates and relative speeds.
script_scope: Teach special chapter patterns by identifying the changing rate: climb-and-slip cycles with a no-final-slip rule, sound distance from hearing delay, maximum/minimum listener separation, moving escalator sum/difference rates, leap-based pursuits, early-arrival pickup time-saving symmetry, mixed-mode return-trip time algebra, and perpendicular motion solved with a right-triangle distance.

name: Data Sufficiency for Time and Distance
description: Decide whether the given motion statements are enough to produce one unique answer.
script_scope: Teach Data Sufficiency using Time and Distance conditions. Cover I-alone, II-alone, both-together, either-alone, and insufficient-even-together reasoning; ratio plus absolute-time data; irrelevant clock information; early/late statements that require combining; equal-distance average-speed questions where an unknown scale cancels; and three-statement redundancy. Test statements independently before combining them.
